source_of_truth: Glickman, 'Example of the Glicko-2 system' (2013), http://www.glicko.net/glicko/glicko2.pdf
periods_elapsed_semantics: periods_elapsed = number of IDLE rating periods (no games) since the last update. Aging is applied FIRST, before the supplied outcomes are processed: phi <- sqrt(phi^2 + periods_elapsed*sigma^2) using the CURRENT (pre-batch) sigma; sigma and rating are unchanged by idle periods. The supplied outcomes[] are the current (active) period and are NOT counted in periods_elapsed (gapless cadence => 0). Empty outcomes => the result is exactly the pre-aged state (the inactivity case). This ordering is mandatory for determinism; do not age after rating.
algorithm: STEP 0 pre-age (idle periods): phi <- sqrt(phi^2 + periods_elapsed*sigma^2)  [sigma, mu unchanged]
inactivity (0 games): phi'=sqrt(phi^2 + periods_elapsed*sigma^2), r' and sigma' unchanged

cases.name: preage_then_batch_ordering
cases.comment: Same games as the paper example but with 1 idle period FIRST. Locks the ordering: RD is inflated to rd_after_preage BEFORE rating the batch (age-then-rate), so RD' ends higher and rating slightly lower than the no-idle paper case (1464.06/151.52). rd_after_preage is exact and is the authoritative ordering check; the final out is a hand-derived reference — regenerate exactly from the reference impl and treat with the loose tolerance below.
